title: Assurance of Salvation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Assurance of salvation is the believer’s Spirit-given confidence that he belongs to Christ and is kept by God’s grace. Assurance rests on God’s promises, Christ’s finished work, the witness of the Spirit, and the fruit of genuine faith.
summary: Assurance of salvation is the believer’s Spirit-given confidence that he belongs to Christ and is kept by God’s grace. Assurance rests on God’s promises, Christ’s finished work, the witness of the Spirit, and the fruit of genuine faith.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the foundation of assurance. Believers are secure not because their faith is flawless, but because Christ saves completely, keeps His sheep, intercedes for His people, and will lose none whom the Father has given Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God does not want His people to live in constant uncertainty about whether Christ is able to save and keep them. Scripture gives believers real grounds for assurance, not in self-confidence, but in the promises and power of God.

Assurance begins with Christ’s finished work. The believer’s hope is not in perfect feelings, perfect obedience, or perfect understanding. The believer looks to Jesus, who died, rose again, intercedes, and keeps His sheep securely in His hand.

The Holy Spirit also bears witness that believers are children of God. He leads them to cry, “Abba, Father,” produces fruit, convicts of sin, strengthens faith, and gives confidence that they belong to God through Christ.

Assurance is not carelessness. Scripture does not give comfort to those who claim Christ while loving sin and refusing repentance. True assurance grows where faith rests in Christ, repentance continues, love for God increases, and the Spirit produces evidence of new life.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers are tormented by fear, shame, past failure, spiritual weakness, or repeated battles with sin. They may think every struggle means they are abandoned by God. Assurance teaches them to look away from unstable feelings and back to the faithful Savior who keeps His people.

This doctrine also protects against false confidence. Assurance is not based on a one-time claim, religious background, emotional moment, or outward appearance. It is grounded in Christ and confirmed by the Spirit’s ongoing work in the life of the believer.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look to Christ as the foundation of your assurance. Do not build your confidence on emotional highs, personal performance, or comparison with others. Examine your life honestly, repent when convicted, trust God’s promises, and ask the Spirit to strengthen your confidence in the Savior who is able to keep you to the end.
